reading.title: Grandma Learns to Use a Computer
reading.text: My grandma is seventy years old. Last month she bought a laptop. At first she was afraid of it. She did not know how to use the mouse and she pressed the wrong keys on the keyboard. Now she writes emails to her friends every day. She has a new email address and she is very proud of it. She also likes sending photos. I save her photos on a memory stick for her. But Grandma still writes letters too. She says a letter is more special than an email. Every Friday she buys a stamp and posts a letter to her sister in Samarkand.

reading.text: Karim got a new phone for his birthday. It has a big screen and a very good camera. He put it in a blue phone case so it will not break. On the first day he downloaded five apps. reading.title: A Holiday in Turkey
reading.text: Last summer Dilnoza and her family went on a package holiday to Turkey. They went by plane. Before the trip, her father checked the passports and the tickets. They also took some Turkish money. The hotel was near the sea. Every morning they swam and in the afternoon they walked in the old town. In the evening the family tried the local food. Dilnoza bought a postcard for her teacher. She also bought a small gift for her friend. After ten days they flew home. Dilnoza says it was the best holiday of her life.

reading.title: Shopping with Mum
reading.text: On Saturday I went shopping with my mum. First we went to the baker and bought two loaves of bread. Then we visited the butcher and got some meat for dinner. After that we went to a big department store. The children's department is on the second floor. I tried on a blue jacket. It was too small, so the shop assistant gave me a bigger size. It cost twenty pounds. Mum paid by card and the assistant gave us a receipt and a carrier bag. We were tired but happy. On the way home we bought a newspaper for Dad at the newsagent.

reading.title: Lisa Shops Online
reading.text: Lisa likes to shop online because it is quick and easy. She does not need to leave her house. Yesterday she looked at a white cotton T-shirt on a website. The price was six pounds ninety nine. She read the reviews and saw that other customers liked it. She chose size small and put two T-shirts in her basket. The total was thirteen pounds ninety eight. Delivery was free, but she had to wait three to five days. She wrote her address and her post code, and she paid with her credit card. Now Lisa is waiting for her order.
